detailed_description: The Gradient Generator is a specialized tool for creating complex CSS gradient syntax through an interactive visual interface. This tool enables developers to generate linear and radial gradients by manipulating direction angles, color stops, and shape parameters in real time. Technically, it converts positional inputs (degrees for linear gradients or radial shapes like ellipse/circle) and color values (HEX, RGB, or HSL) into standardized CSS gradient notation. Users benefit from immediate visual feedback as they adjust transition points, allowing precise control over gradient stops, midpoints, and directionality. The generator accounts for browser compatibility by outputting gradients in both modern syntax and legacy vendor-prefixed versions when necessary. Developers working on UI components like buttons, background overlays, or card elements can rapidly prototype gradients without manual CSS calculations, eliminating trial-and-error coding. Advanced features include opacity control sliders, color format conversion, and the ability to export gradients as reusable CSS classes.
usage_steps: Select gradient type using the 'Linear' or 'Radial' radio buttons
Adjust direction angle via the degree input field or drag the directional handle in the live preview
Click '+ Add Stop' to insert color stops at specific percentage positions along the gradient line
Use the color picker pop-up to select hues for each stop, with real-time updates to the gradient visualization
Toggle 'CSS Preview' to view generated code with vendor prefixes and class structure
Copy the complete CSS gradient declaration to clipboard for immediate implementation
usage_examples: Creating a diagonal hero section background with a 135-degree linear gradient transitioning from #FFD700 to #FF69B4
Designing a subtle button hover effect using a 10% opacity radial gradient overlay on a dark background
Generating a material design-style card shadow using a 50% radial gradient with transparent black color stops
Implementing a dark mode transition effect with a vertical linear gradient from #1A1A1A to #2C2C2C
